deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT (from the previous page, corrected against the algebra). This is Riemann's normal form for a plane quartic (genus p=3), sqrt(x*xi)+sqrt(y*eta)+sqrt(z*zeta)=0. Here x,y,z,xi,eta,zeta are six bitangent linear forms subject to:
(R1) x+y+z+xi+eta+zeta=0
(R2) xi/alpha+eta/beta+zeta/gamma+alpha*x+beta*y+gamma*z=0
(R3) the same with alpha',beta',gamma'.

The author has already identified the Abelian function (root of a bitangent) of characteristic (p+e). It is sqrt(v), with
 v = alpha*x+eta/beta+zeta/gamma = -(xi/alpha+beta*y+gamma*z)   (this is R2).

The algebra only closes if the auxiliary forms are (my reconstruction; the transcription garbles them):
 t = x+y+z = -(xi+eta+zeta)
 u = xi+eta+z = -(x+y+zeta)   (both by R1).

Eliminating zeta, z and then eta, y from v+u/gamma and v+gamma*u gives
 v = u(beta-gamma)/(1-beta*gamma) + x*beta(1-alpha*gamma)/(1-beta*gamma) - (xi/alpha)(1-alpha*gamma)/(1-beta*gamma).

The analogous elimination with t, using gamma(v-alpha*t) - alpha(v-t/alpha), gives
 v = t(1-alpha*gamma)/(alpha-gamma) + (eta/beta)(beta-gamma)/(alpha-gamma) - alpha*y(beta-gamma)/(alpha-gamma).

Hence
 v = a*t+b'*eta+c*y = -(a'*u+b*x+c'*xi)
with
 a=(1-ag)/(a-g), a'=-(b-g)/(1-bg), b=-b(1-ag)/(1-bg), b'=(b-g)/(b(a-g)), c=-a(b-g)/(a-g), c'=(1-ag)/(a(1-bg)).
By the earlier general result (eq. 22) this yields four Abelian functions:
 sqrt(at+bx+cy)=sqrt(-(a'u+b'eta+c'xi)), with characteristic (kappa1)
 sqrt(a'u+bx+cy)=sqrt(-(at+b'eta+c'xi)), with characteristic (kappa2)
 plus sqrt(v) and one more.

THIS PAGE.

(1) Characteristic (kappa1). Substitute t=x+y+z into at+bx+cy. The coefficients become:
 x: (1-ag)(1-ab)/((a-g)(1-bg))
 y: (1-ab)/(a-g)
 z: (1-ag)/(a-g)
Dividing by (1-ab)(1-ag)/(a-g) gives
 w1 = x/(1-bg)+y/(1-ga)+z/(1-ab).
Substitute u=xi+eta+z into -(a'u+b'eta+c'xi). The coefficients become:
 xi: -(1-ab)/(a(1-bg))
 eta: -(b-g)(1-ab)/(b(1-bg)(a-g))
 z: (b-g)/(1-bg)
Multiplying by (1-bg)/((1-ab)(b-g)) gives
 w1' = xi/(a(g-b))+eta/(b(g-a))+z/(1-ab).
Both match the page.

(2) Characteristic (kappa2). Substitute t=-(xi+eta+zeta) into -(at+b'eta+c'xi). The coefficients become:
 xi: (1-ag)g(1-ab)/(a(a-g)(1-bg))
 eta: g(1-ab)/(b(a-g))
 zeta: (1-ag)/(a-g)
Normalising gives
 w2 = xi/(a(1-bg))+eta/(b(1-ga))+zeta/(g(1-ab)).
Substitute u=-(x+y+zeta) into a'u+bx+cy. The coefficients become:
 x: -g(1-ab)/(1-bg)
 y: -g(b-g)(1-ab)/((a-g)(1-bg))
 zeta: (b-g)/(1-bg)
Normalising gives
 w2' = x/(g-b)+y/(g-a)+zeta/(g(1-ab)).
Both match the page. The phrase 'bis auf Unterdrückung constanter Factoren' refers exactly to these normalisations.

(3) The functions for (kappa1'),(kappa2'),(kappa1''),(kappa2'') follow by replacing (alpha,beta,gamma) with the primed or double-primed constants. The previous page shows these characteristics arise from the forms (q+f),(q+g), etc.

(4) For the earlier numerical choice of the basic characteristics, the six characteristics are listed as 2x3 binary matrices. All are odd, as bitangent characteristics must be.

(5) The double-primed constants are expressible through alpha,beta,gamma,alpha',beta',gamma' (shown earlier). Hence all 28 Abelian functions (bitangents) and their algebraic relations depend on 3p-3=6 constants. These are the moduli of the class for p=3.
errors: Possible slip or misreading in the characteristic table. As transcribed, (kappa2')=(011;010) coincides with (kappa1''), but distinct bitangents must have distinct characteristics.

Consistency check on the table. The quadruple structure of the previous page, kappa1+kappa2+(p+e)+(q+e)=0 etc., forces kappa1+kappa2 = kappa1'+kappa2' = kappa1''+kappa2'' (= p+q). The first two sums give (001;000), but the transcribed kappa1''+kappa2'' = (101;000). Reading kappa1''=(111;010) would restore consistency. Whether the slip is in the manuscript or the transcription cannot be decided without the earlier example.

Not an error but a caveat. The two expressions given for the same characteristic, e.g. w1 and w1', are not identical modulo R1, R2 alone. Their identification as one Abelian function rests on the earlier general result (eq. 22) and on the third relation, which this page does not verify.
The algebra on this page is otherwise correct. All four displayed linear forms follow exactly from the coefficients a..c' derived on the previous page, given t=x+y+z and u=xi+eta+z.

results.what: Explicit expressions for the bitangents with characteristics kappa1, kappa2 (and by substitution their primed and double-primed analogues) in Riemann's normal form sqrt(x xi)+sqrt(y eta)+sqrt(z zeta)=0, e.g. x/(1-bg)+y/(1-ga)+z/(1-ab) and xi/(a(1-bg))+eta/(b(1-ga))+zeta/(g(1-ab)).
results.modern_name: Riemann's equations for the 28 bitangents of a plane quartic from an Aronhold set (Riemann normal form)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (lectures c. 1861-62, published posthumously in Werke 1876, 'Zur Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen für den Fall p=3'); developed by Weber (1876), Aronhold (1864)

results.what: Assignment of odd theta characteristics to the bitangents in a worked example
results.modern_name: Correspondence between the 28 odd theta characteristics and the 28 bitangents of a genus-3 curve

results.what: All Abelian functions of a genus-3 class expressed through 6 constants alpha,beta,gamma,alpha',beta',gamma', identified as the 3p-3 moduli
results.modern_name: dim M_3 = 3g-3 = 6; moduli of plane quartics via Aronhold sets

deep.surprise_reason: This is the material of Riemann's p=3 theory as published in his Werke (1876) and treated by Weber. The page is a careful working-out of known formulas, with no result beyond what is credited to Riemann.

transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'bis auf [?] Unterdrückung' should read 'bis auf Unterdrückung'.
In the second kappa1 expression the last term is indeed z/(1-alpha*beta) (Latin z, not zeta); the algebra confirms this.
Previous page: u must be xi+eta+z = -x-y-zeta (not xi+eta+zeta = -x-y-z). The auxiliary t is x+y+z = -(xi+eta+zeta).
Previous page: in 'v = u(β-γ)/(1-βγ)+x...-ζ/α ...' the last variable is xi, not zeta: -(xi/alpha)(1-alpha*gamma)/(1-beta*gamma).
Previous page: 'v = at+b'y+cy = -a'u-bx-c'ζ' should be v = a t + b' eta + c y = -a' u - b x - c' xi. Similarly, the four Abelian functions use b'eta and c'xi.
Characteristic table: (kappa1'') is transcribed as (011;010), identical to (kappa2'). Consistency with kappa1+kappa2 = kappa1'+kappa2' = (001;000) suggests (kappa1'')=(111;010). Re-examine the image.
